The Island of Nature, Sea and Timeless Beauty

Sardinia

Sardinia is one of the most extraordinary islands of the Mediterranean — a place where pristine nature, ancient culture and a unique way of life have remained preserved for centuries.

Surrounded by the deep blue waters of the Mediterranean Sea, the island is famous for its crystal-clear coastline, dramatic landscapes, exceptional cuisine and extraordinary biodiversity.

Sardinia is not only a destination of beauty. It is a place where nature defines the rhythm of life.

Crystal Waters and Untouched Coastlines

The Mediterranean Sea

The sea surrounding Sardinia is considered one of the clearest and most beautiful in the Mediterranean.

The coastline is shaped by hundreds of kilometres of beaches, hidden bays, granite cliffs and turquoise lagoons.

The exceptional transparency of the water reveals a rich underwater world:

  • protected marine areas
  • sea grass meadows
  • rocky underwater landscapes
  • diverse Mediterranean marine life

The famous colours of Sardinian waters — from emerald green to deep sapphire blue — are created by the combination of pure water, white sand, granite formations and intense Mediterranean sunlight.

The sea is not only a natural treasure of Sardinia, but also the central element of its identity.

Between Mountains, Granite and Sea

The Landscapes of Sardinia

The beauty of Sardinia lies in the extraordinary diversity of its landscapes. The island combines:

  • ancient mountains
  • wild Mediterranean forests
  • granite cliffs
  • hidden beaches
  • valleys covered with aromatic plants
  • coastal landscapes shaped by wind and time

Unlike many Mediterranean destinations, large areas of Sardinia remain untouched, preserving a feeling of authenticity and natural freedom.

Every region of the island has its own character, but the northern part — Gallura — is especially remarkable for its dramatic geology and unique atmosphere.

The Land of Pink Granite and Mediterranean Light

Gallura

Gallura is the historic region of north-eastern Sardinia, famous for its monumental granite landscapes, emerald sea and characteristic Mediterranean vegetation.

The landscape of Gallura was shaped over millions of years by geological processes and the power of wind and water. Huge formations of pink granite emerge throughout the territory, creating natural sculptures with soft rounded forms.

This granite became one of the defining symbols of the region. Its warm colours — from pale rose to golden beige — change throughout the day depending on the sunlight, creating a constantly transforming landscape.

The architecture of Gallura developed in harmony with this environment, using local stone and respecting the natural forms of the land.

The Mediterranean Garden

The Vegetation of Gallura

The vegetation of northern Sardinia is one of its greatest natural treasures. The landscape is dominated by characteristic Mediterranean plants.

Juniper

Ancient juniper trees with twisted forms grow among rocks and coastal areas. Their sculptural shapes are one of the most recognizable elements of the Sardinian landscape.

Myrtle

A traditional Mediterranean plant with aromatic leaves and delicate white flowers. Myrtle has a special cultural importance in Sardinia and is used to produce the famous local liqueur Mirto.

Strawberry Tree (Arbutus unedo)

An evergreen Mediterranean tree with beautiful foliage, white flowers and bright red fruits appearing in autumn.

Olive Trees

Ancient olive trees represent the connection between Sardinian landscape, agriculture and tradition.

Lavender, Rosemary and Wild Herbs

The island air is filled with the aromas of native plants, creating the unique atmosphere of the Mediterranean maquis.

In Gallura, gardens are often designed as extensions of the natural landscape, combining cultivated plants with wild vegetation.

A Cuisine Created by Nature

The Flavours of Sardinia

Sardinian cuisine reflects the island itself — simple, authentic and based on exceptional local products. The Mediterranean climate and traditional agriculture create ingredients of remarkable quality:

  • fresh seafood
  • locally produced olive oil
  • artisan cheeses
  • traditional breads
  • herbs from the wild landscape
  • vegetables and fruits grown under the Sardinian sun

The cuisine of Gallura is especially connected with the sea and rural traditions, combining fishermen's recipes with ancient pastoral culture.

Food in Sardinia is not only a culinary experience — it is part of the island's cultural heritage.

Around Costa Paradiso

Cities and Places Nearby

Santa Teresa Gallura

Located at the northernmost point of Sardinia, Santa Teresa Gallura is one of the most beautiful coastal towns of the region.

Founded in the nineteenth century, the town is known for its elegant central square, views towards Corsica, dramatic cliffs and beautiful beaches.

The nearby Capo Testa peninsula is famous for enormous granite formations shaped by wind and sea, creating one of the most spectacular landscapes in Gallura.

Distance from Costa Paradiso: approximately 35–40 minutes by car

Luogosanto

Situated inland among granite hills and Mediterranean forests, Luogosanto represents the traditional soul of Gallura. The town is surrounded by ancient landscapes, vineyards, cork oak forests and historical sites.

The area is known for:

  • rural traditions
  • granite architecture
  • churches and ancient sanctuaries
  • peaceful countryside landscapes

Luogosanto offers a different vision of Sardinia — quiet, authentic and deeply connected with nature.

Distance from Costa Paradiso: approximately 30 minutes by car

Castelsardo

One of the most beautiful medieval towns of Sardinia, Castelsardo rises dramatically above the sea on a volcanic promontory. Its ancient fortress, narrow streets and panoramic views create an atmosphere where history and landscape merge together.

The town is famous for:

  • the medieval castle of the Doria family
  • traditional crafts
  • breathtaking views of the northern coastline
  • sunsets over the Mediterranean Sea

Castelsardo represents the historical and cultural heritage of northern Sardinia.

Distance from Costa Paradiso: approximately 50–60 minutes by car

Sardinia — A Philosophy of Life

Sardinia offers something increasingly rare in the modern world: a connection with nature, time and authenticity.

Here, architecture follows the landscape, gardens grow together with wild vegetation, and daily life remains connected with the rhythms of the Mediterranean.

The island's greatest luxury is not excess, but harmony — the possibility of living surrounded by pure sea, ancient stone, Mediterranean light and landscapes that have preserved their original beauty for centuries.
